name: Telegram Samsung Backup Bot app fpr mac
prompt:
Telegram Samsung Backup Bot app fpr mac

Local-first Python utility that scans a Samsung Smart Switch backup, mirrors each top-level folder into a Telegram forum topic, creates ≤700 MB zip chunks, and posts the chunks into the correct topics via a Telegram bot the user controls.
Why this project exists

    Keep Smart Switch backups redundantly stored in Telegram without manual uploads.
    Maintain a one-to-one mapping between backup folders and forum topics for easier navigation.
    Support resumable runs and dry-runs so large uploads remain predictable.

High-level plan

    Prepare Telegram – promote the bot as admin, enable topics, grab the forum chat id, and record the bot token in .env.
    Configure the bot – point BACKUP_ROOT, WORK_DIR, chunk size, and retry options via .env or CLI flags.
    Scan backup folders – BackupScanner inventories every top-level folder under the Smart Switch directory, collecting size and file metadata.
    Ensure topics exist – TelegramService uses a JSON topic registry to reuse or create forum topics whose names match folder names.
    Chunk + zip – Chunker walks each folder, creates sequential zip archives that never exceed 700 MB, and stores manifests for resume support.
    Upload chunks – Uploader streams each archive to the matching topic with retries, captioning each message with chunk info and checksums.
    Verify + repeat – rerun python -m backup_bot.main to resume unfinished uploads, clean up temp files, and review logs.

Project structure

tgbot/
├── README.md
├── pyproject.toml
├── .env.example
├── backup_bot/
│   ├── __init__.py
│   ├── main.py
│   ├── config.py
│   ├── logger.py
│   └── services/
│       ├── __init__.py
│       ├── backup_scanner.py
│       ├── chunker.py
│       ├── telegram_client.py
│       └── uploader.py
└── tests/
    └── test_chunker.py

Configuration

Copy .env.example to .env and fill in the values:

TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=123456:ABC...
TELEGRAM_FORUM_CHAT_ID=-1001234567890
BACKUP_ROOT=C:/Users/you/Samsung/SmartSwitch/backup
WORK_DIR=./.backup_work
MAX_CHUNK_MB=700
DRY_RUN=false

You can override any of these at runtime:

python -m backup_bot.main --backup-root "D:/Samsung" --work-dir "./.backup_work" --dry-run

Telegram Backup Bot

    Default chunk size is set to 45 MB to comply with Telegram Bot API document upload limits (~50 MB). Override via .env:

MAX_CHUNK_MB=45

    To use larger sizes (e.g. 700 MB), you must upload via user accounts or alternative APIs. For this bot (Bot API), keep chunks <= 50 MB.

Quick Start

cd tgbot
python -m backup_bot.main --bot

Configure .env:

TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=...
TELEGRAM_FORUM_CHAT_ID=https://t.me/c/<id>/1
BACKUP_ROOT=C:\Users\nah\Samsung\SmartSwitch\backup\...
WORK_DIR=.backup_work
MAX_CHUNK_MB=45

Running the bot

    Ensure the Telegram bot is admin and the group is converted to a forum.
    Create/activate a virtualenv, install dependencies, and populate .env.
    Run the script:

    python -m backup_bot.main

    Monitor the console logs for progress. Every upload prints the folder/topic/chunk.
    When using bot mode, interact via Telegram:
        /listfolders – scan Smart Switch folders and display numbered options.
        /pickfolder <n> – choose which folder index to resume from; the bot remembers until the next run.
        /startbackup – begin uploading starting from the selected folder.
        /stopbackup, /forcebackupstop, /backupstatus – runtime controls.

Implementation notes

    Chunk manifests live in WORK_DIR/manifests/<folder>.json so reruns skip completed uploads.
    Topic registry at WORK_DIR/topics.json prevents duplicate topics.
    Dry run skips compression/upload and only logs planned actions.
    Tenacity retries back off automatically on network hiccups or Telegram rate limits.

Testing

pip install -e .[dev]
pytest

tests/test_chunker.py verifies the chunking algorithm respects the size ceiling and naming scheme.
Next steps / enhancements

    Encrypt archives before uploading (e.g., pyzipper.AESZipFile).
    Parallelize uploads per topic for faster runs.
    Track SHA256 per chunk and emit a verification report.
    Add a small UI to select folders and show upload history.

plan.techStack: Swift 5.9, SwiftUI, SwiftData, FSEvents, CryptoKit, MTProto Swift, macOS 14+
steps: Configure macOS app project with SwiftUI lifecycle, App Sandbox entitlements, and user-selected file read/write permissions
Implement SecureBookmark utility to persist folder access permissions across app restarts using bookmark data
Define SwiftData schema entities for SyncFolder, FileRecord, and TopicMapping with proper relationships and indexing
Build FileMonitor service using FSEvents to detect live filesystem changes in monitored directories
Develop Chunker service with CryptoKit AES-256 encryption and per-file SHA-256 hashing for 700MB zip archives
Implement MTProtoClient service for User API authentication, session persistence, and chunked upload support
Create SyncEngine orchestrator to debounce FSEvents, manage upload queues, and handle resume logic via SwiftData
Build topic management system to flatten folder paths into Telegram forum topic names with hash-based collision avoidance
Develop SwiftUI interface with folder list display, per-folder progress indicators, and dry-run toggle
Add comprehensive error handling with exponential backoff for Telegram FloodWait and network resilience
plan.architectNotes: Native macOS Swift app replacing Python utility; leverages MTProto User API for 700MB uploads, SwiftData for atomic state management, FSEvents for continuous monitoring, and SecureBookmarks for persistent folder access across restarts
plan.reviewerNotes: Clarify scope as unidirectional backup vs bidirectional sync; implement truncated hashed topic names to avoid Telegram 128-character limit; MTProto phone authentication adds deployment complexity versus simple Bot API tokens
